title: Probabilistic kernel hedging for prefill-decode pipelines
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a probabilistic hedging layer in the runtime kernel selector that can safely mix conservative low-latency kernels with higher-throughput kernels based on per-request sequence-length forecasts and short online probes. Goal: reduce unit token cost while keeping P95/P99 latency SLOs for conversational workloads and graceful fallbacks during sudden bursts or model/arch mismatches. This ticket covers design, microbench harness, simulation, and an end-to-end rollout plan into the canary runtime cluster.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Hedging controller implemented in runtime selector with feature flag. 2) Offline simulator demonstrates >=8% average token-cost reduction on production request trace while P95 latency does not regress by more than 10% and P99 remains within SLO. 3) End-to-end integration tests (unit + e2e) covering warm-start probes, rollback on latency excursions, and correct telemetry emission. 4) Canary rollout plan documented and ready, with dashboards/alerts configured.
notes: 2025-02-12 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after architecture sync. Motivation: mixed conversational loads show long-tail latency spikes when runtime switches to high-throughput kernels for long prefill sequences. Proposal: use a hedging policy that keeps a small percentage of requests on conservative kernels while probing candidates for warm-starts.

2025-02-15 Diego Morales: Spike completed - profiled kernels across T4/A10G/V100 for sequence buckets (<=64, 65-256, >256). Observations: some quantized kernels reduce cost by 15% but increase P99 for >512 tokens. Need online probe budget cap to avoid tail amplification.

2025-02-19 Design decision: Use a Thompson-sampling style bandit where reward is negative-cost but penalized by latency-exceed events. Maintain exponential decay for historical observations to adapt to drift. Store per-arch, per-model, per-seqlen-bucket statistics keyed by (arch, model-sha, seqlen-bucket).

2025-02-23 Implementation note: Added microbenchmark harness in github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-probes/pull/187 (WIP). Harness supports configurable noise injection and synthetic KV cache priming to emulate conversational prefill-decode patterns.

2025-02-26 Telemetry spec: emit hedging_event with fields: chosen_kernel, candidate_kernel, seqlen_bucket, probe_result_ms, tokens, cost_estimate_cents. Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RUN/pages/Kernel+Hedging+Design (draft)

2025-03-01 Simulation results: ran simulator against 48 hours production trace (sampled). Hedging with 5% conservative retention + 10% probe rate achieved 9.1% token-cost reduction; P95 increased 6.7% overall, P99 increased 3.4% (within acceptance target). Cost reduction concentrated in seqlen 65-256 buckets.

2025-03-03 Risk/Trade-offs: Probing increases variance; important to cap probe rate and use backoff per-request-id to avoid repeated probes on same session. Also need to ensure probes are routed to compatible model variant (same quantization/ops) to avoid decode failures.

2025-03-04 Next steps: finalize rollout playbook, build canary dashboards (latency by kernel, hedging_event success/failure), add security review for telemetry schema, and land PR for hedging controller. Assigned Diego to finish PR and pair with infra for canary resources.
